To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a heavy singlet Higgs, arising from the production of vector-like quarks, can give rise to a ( 6 b 2 ℓ ± 2 ℏ t ¯ ) signal at the LHC, with a large cross section, which is free of the Standard Model backgrounds.
a singlet Higg and down-type vector-like quarks can be discovered at the LHC through the ( 2 b + 4 t ) final state.
a heavy singlet Higgs arising from a down-type vector-like quark decay gives rise to a signal that can be detected in the LHC run-2.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the search for the production of a pair of heavy down type vector-like (V) quarks, V, which decay to a pair of a Higgs boson, H, and a top quark, t, with the subsequent decay of the Higgs boson to a pair of down type quarks, q q, and that of top quark to a b and a W +.
the study of the phenomenology of the Higgs boson in the light of its possible production in association with vector-like quarks and its subsequent decay to two b quarks.
the search of a heavy Higgs boson in the decay of a pair of vector-like quarks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the singlet Higgs model with vector-like quarks is a viable candidate for explaining the excesses in the 3.2 fb − 1 data of the CMS collaboration in the 2 b 2 t channel.
the singlet Higgs scenario with vector-like quarks can be probed at the LHC, and the signal can be distinguished from the background with the present experimental setup.
the signal is very promising and the background is negligible, which makes the search for such a signal at the LHC a very exciting prospect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a singlet heavy Higs can be searched for by the production and decay to the vector-like quark pair at the Large Hadron collider.

, if the current Higgs data is interpreted as arising from the production of the singlet heavy scalar, then a signal for the vector-like quark would be observed at the 14 TeV run of the Large Hadron Collider.
the singlet Higgs can be observed through its decay to the heavy vector-like fermion pair and the subsequent decay of the heavy fermion to a pair of Standard Model quarks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current LHC data does not exclude such a scenario and the 14 Te V run of the LHC is expected to be able to probe the parameter space of the model.
